Last Thursday (Nov 12, 2026), the ingest pipeline stalled for 3h40: ingest v2.14.0 (PR ingest#412) raised the default `max_batch_bytes` from 1 MB to 10 MB, and with the pods' 512 Mi memory limit the ingest-worker pods ran out of memory on the first large batch and crash-looped, so events piled up in Kafka and customer dashboards went stale between 08:47 and 12:27 UTC [1]. The change went to all pods at once; there was no consumer-lag alert, so the first signal was a Sentry OOM alert 27 minutes after the deploy [1]. Rollback to v2.13.3 at 10:05 drained the backlog by 12:27 [1].

No customer data was lost: events kept arriving in Kafka and were only processed late — the Nov 13 reconciliation matched per-workspace event counts to Kafka offsets for 08:00–13:00 UTC, "nothing lost, just late" [1][7]. Impact was limited to delayed dashboards across all workspaces; 4 customers contacted support (Orbitly, Zest Grocers, 2 trial accounts) [1].

What we're changing (postmortem action items) [1]:
- KES-431 – page on-call when ingest consumer lag exceeds 5 minutes (Noa, due Nov 20) [1][4]
- KES-432 – ingest config changes go to a canary pool first (Daniel, due Nov 27) [1]
- KES-433 – raise worker memory limit to 1 Gi and add a load test on batch sizes (Lior, due Nov 27) [1]
- Plus ingest#419 (merged Nov 13): `max_batch_bytes` default back to 1 MB, and the batcher refuses any batch larger than 25% of the container memory limit, with 10 MB kept only on the explicit bulk-import path [16]

The same fixes were communicated to Orbitly in the Nov 15 incident report from Maya [3]. One side note: Orbitly is claiming an SLA service credit for the incident under section 7 of their MSA, and Sam is checking the terms with finance [3].
